To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
TEA induced transient tetanic contractions of the rabbit coronary arteries as a result of spontaneous Ca-spike discharges.
the vasoactive effects of tetraethylamonium on helical strips of rabbit coronary artery were tested and found to be due to spontaneous Ca-spike discharges in smooth muscle.
the vasoactive effect and underlying mechanisms of TEA on rabbit coronary artery are similar to those on arterial and trachealis muscle.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the vasoactivity of the well-known K channel blockers.
the vasoactive effect induced by tetraethylammonoium (TEA) on helical strips isolated from the large epicardi coronary arteries of rabbit heart.
the effects of tetraethyl ammonium (TEA) on the contractility of the coronary artery.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
TEA induces a contraction in the rabbit coronary artery as a result of spontaneous Ca-spikes and that this contraction is mediated by Ca-influx through the voltage-gated Ca-channels.
the vasoactive effect induced by TEA is a result of spontaneous Ca-spikes and the subsequent Ca-entry, which is not mediated by the K channel.
the vasoactive effect and mechanism of action of tetraethyl-ammonium are not uniform in all types of smooth muscle.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the K channel blockers, such as TEA and Cs+, are not only useful tools to study K channels, but also to study Ca-spike discharge and its role in contraction of vascular smooth muscle.

the rabbit coronary artery, like the arterial smooth muscle of other species, is capable of spontaneous Ca-spike activity and that TEA-induced tetanic contraction is due to summation of twitch response caused by Ca-spikes.

the K channel blocker, TEA, induces spontaneous Ca-spike activity and tetanic contraction of the rabbit large coronary artery, and the spontaneous Ca-spike is mediated by Ca entry through the L-type Ca channel.
The main takeaway from our work is that
TEA-induced contractions are not due to the blockade of Ca-activated K channels but to the inhibition of Ca-activated Cl channels.
the vasoactive effect and mechanism of TEA-induced contraction in the rabbit coronary artery are similar to those reported in other arterial and trachea smooth muscle.
